# `scripts/post-process/check_compressed_halos.py`

Source: [check_compressed_halos.py](../../../../scripts/post-process/check_compressed_halos.py)

check\_compressed\_halos.py: independent check of compress\_halo\_outputs.py results against the ASCII files.

Parses the ASCII with numpy (not pandas, which the converter uses) and requires, for every column:
int64 columns equal exactly, float64 columns equal exactly, float32 columns equal float32(ASCII value).
Also checks .vahc alignment, readers.py-style access (ConvertToFITS.fits\_to\_record), tree files, the
FitsRow index of locations.fits.gz and forests.fits.gz, and that the headers read back (with the run's
SIM\_STEM, SIM\_REAL, SIM\_IC\_SEED). Run it before deleting any ASCII file.

usage: check\_compressed\_halos.py &lt;run dir with out\_\*.trees&gt; [--snaps 0,5,99] [--outdir DIR] [--trees] [--nproc N]

## Contents

- [`ok`](#ok) - Print PASS/FAIL `msg` and count failures in the global `bad`.
- [`same`](#same) - True if FITS column `v` equals the text-table values `a` at the column's precision (int64, float64 exactly, float32 after rounding; NaNs equal).
- [`check_snapshot`](#check_snapshot) - Compare the FITS tables of snapshot `snap` in `out` with the text outputs in run directory `R`: row counts, every column, header cards and checksums.
- [`tree_plan`](#tree_plan) - [(FITS tree file, [(ASCII tree file, first row, rows or None)])]: one tree\_X\_Y\_Z.fits.gz per tree\_X\_Y\_Z.dat, or the merged tree\_0\_0\_0.fits.gz (header MERGED, TILEnnnn cards) holding several.
- [`ascii_tree_chunks`](#ascii_tree_chunks) - Rows of a tree\_X\_Y\_Z.dat parsed with numpy (independent of the converter's pandas), chunk lines at a time.
- [`check_trees`](#check_trees) - Every tree file against the ASCII, both read a chunk at a time (memory bounded: the tree files of a 2048^3 run hold ~1e9 rows); the FITS file through C.StreamTable (its DATASUMs checked too). Then locations (FitsRow, FitsRows select exactly each tree: a run of equal Tree\_root\_ID starting there, of that length) and forests.
- [`_task`](#_task) - One snapshot (or 'trees') in a worker: its PASS/FAIL lines and failure count.
- [`main`](#main) - Command line (see `--help`): check the compressed halo tables and trees of a run directory; exits non-zero on any failure.

## ok

```python
ok(cond, msg)
```

Print PASS/FAIL `msg` and count failures in the global `bad`.

## same

```python
same(v, a)
```

True if FITS column `v` equals the text-table values `a` at the column's precision (int64, float64
exactly, float32 after rounding; NaNs equal).

## check_snapshot

```python
check_snapshot(R, out, snap)
```

Compare the FITS tables of snapshot `snap` in `out` with the text outputs in run directory `R`:
row counts, every column, header cards and checksums.

## check_trees

```python

```

Every tree file against the ASCII, both read a chunk at a time (memory bounded: the tree files of a 2048^3 run
hold ~1e9 rows); the FITS file through C.StreamTable (its DATASUMs checked too). Then locations (FitsRow,
FitsRows select exactly each tree: a run of equal Tree\_root\_ID starting there, of that length) and forests.
